fixtures.preview: A battered United side head to Anfield for the biggest rivalry in English football (4:30pm UK, 3:30am Mon 23 Nov Sydney), still chasing a first league win since August.
talking_points: United drew 4-4 at home to Aston Villa on Sunday after trailing 2-0 twice, Patrick Dorgu heading in the equaliser in the 96th minute.
Sky Sports has United in the relegation zone after 10 games and without a Premier League win since August, with Michael Carrick under pressure.
Carrick called the goals conceded 'totally avoidable'; no injury or suspension news has been reported since, so team news is unconfirmed until closer to kick-off.
In Europe United beat Roma 3-2 on 3 Nov, but lost 4-1 at Como and 2-0 at Atlético earlier in the league phase.

fixtures.preview: Matchday 5 in Lisbon: United have 6 points from 4 games and need a result to stay in the top-eight race (21:00 CET, 7am Thu 26 Nov Sydney).
Brentford visit Old Trafford on Saturday 28 Nov at 3pm UK time (2am Sun 29 Nov Sydney).
A Wednesday-night trip to Tyneside at 8pm UK time (7am Thu 3 Dec Sydney); Sky lists the time but the schedule is subject to change.
Newly promoted Coventry visit Old Trafford on Saturday 5 Dec at 3pm UK time (2am Sun 6 Dec Sydney).
Sydney travel to Brisbane (6:40pm Brisbane time, 7:40pm Sydney) off a 4-1 home win over Central Coast.
talking_points: Al Hassan Toure hit a hat-trick in the 4-1 win over the Mariners, and coach Patrick Kisnorbo says 'the best is yet to come'.
Jacob Farrell, on loan from Portsmouth, was expected to debut against his former club Central Coast, so he may be pushing for a regular place.
Abel Walatee (ankle) and Jake Hollman (hamstring) were out in the latest club squad news; their availability for Brisbane is unconfirmed.
Gus Hoefsloot has recovered from a pre-season wrist injury and is available again.

fixtures.preview: The Big Blue at Allianz Stadium on Sunday 6 December at 5pm.
An away game in Auckland in round 8, listed at 5pm (treated here as New Zealand time).

notes: Many club, venue and supermarket pages were unreadable or dynamic, so some details come from search results or third-party listings and are flagged in the item text.

Man Utd: kick-offs come from Liverpool FC (Liverpool game), UEFA and Sky Sports. Stan Sport as broadcaster for Premier League and Champions League games rests on its existing Australian rights and was not confirmed for each match.
Man Utd v Aston Villa finished 4-4 on Sun 8 Nov (Sky Sports, Aston Villa site). I found no injury or suspension news for Liverpool, so team news is unconfirmed.

Sydney FC: the Brisbane talking points are from the club's 5 Nov squad-news page. I couldn't open the latest result or ladder page, so no table position is given. The Auckland kick-off is treated as New Zealand time.

Big matches: Champions League kick-offs use UEFA's default 21:00 CET; broadcasters for those games were not re-confirmed. The Jordan v Socceroos friendly (17 Nov local) has no confirmed time, so it isn't listed.

Local: no local news from the last 7 days was found, and the City of Sydney suburb pages for Redfern, Waterloo, Erskineville and Eveleigh didn't load. School events come from the Term 4 calendars and Week 4 Principal Updates (dates may change). Nothing was found for the second school or for South Eveleigh this month. The Alexandria Christmas Concert is on 13 Dec, outside this window.

Arts: Whispering Jack dates and price come from search results (the STC page blocked access). Spacey Jane (Sydney Opera House Forecourt, 10–11 Dec) and Hoodoo Gurus (reported for 5 Dec) are just outside the 4-week window and not confirmed on a ticketing page.
Live sport: no Sydney tennis, rugby union or Matildas games were found for the next 4 weeks. Other Kings dates were not confirmed; some listings name the arena Afterpay Arena.
Son and daughter: nothing found for Sydney Pokémon, Minecraft or Roblox events, a junior parkrun, matcha pop-ups or author or book events in the next 4 weeks.

Groceries: store sites blocked access. Supermarket item lists come from catalogue sites, with no was-prices for most; the Coles and Woolworths 11–17 Nov catalogues are mostly images, so the list of half-price lines is short. Items marked as ending 10 Nov finish today.
Horizon: the Asian Cup was moved on 3 Nov to 23 Dec 2027–21 Jan 2028 (subject to FIFA approval). Diana Ross is new; BTS at Accor Stadium (reported for 20–21 Feb 2027) was not confirmed.
